sourceFacts.fact: In people with psoriasis, skin injury may be followed by a new psoriatic lesion at that same site.
The relationship is temporal and spatial; the response is not inevitable.

nodes.label: New psoriasis at the same site

labels: Koebner phenomenon: same site, later lesion
New psoriasis at the same site
layout: Three large side-by-side panels. First and third each contain the EXACT SAME neutral 3-by-3 grid of ivory paper squares. In first panel put a small coral X on the central square; in third replace that X with a single purple circular token on the central square. Other eight squares stay blank in BOTH grids. Middle panel shows a simple clock. Exactly two arrows from panel1 to2 to3. Under first grid say Injury marker; under third say Lesion marker. Caption: A matched-location concept, not a skin image. Small note: May occur after injury in psoriasis. No texture resembling skin, scales, rash, scratches, blood or body parts. These are coordinate grids only.

requiredChecks: Both grids exactly three by three
Only the central square is marked in each grid
Injury marker becomes lesion marker at same location after an interval
No anatomical skin or clinical lesion simulation
validation.pixelChecks: Pixel check: both panels contain exactly three-by-three grids; only central square marked, X first and purple lesion token later. Clock between panels and two forward arrows preserve same-site delayed relation. No clinical skin depiction; possible occurrence qualifier clear. Independent and clinical review pending.
